annotations.title: The foundation of penance.
annotations.text: ◦ We see hereby, what the first groundes of Christian institution or Catechisme were in the primitiue Church, and that there was euer a necessarie instruction and beleefe of certaine points had by word of mouth and tradition, before men came to the Scriptures: which could not treate of things so particularly, as was requisite for the teaching of al necessarie groundes. Among these points were the 12 Articles conteined in the Apostles Creede: the doctrine of penance before Baptisme: the maner and necessitie of Baptisme: the Sacrament of Imposition of hands after Baptisme, called Confirmation: the articles of the Resurrection, Iudgement, and such like. Without which things first laid, if one should be sent to picke his faith out of the Scripture, there would be madde rule quickly. See S. Augustine in expost. inchoat. ep. ad Ro. versus finem.

notes.text: The Apostles forme of Catechisme, and the points therof.

annotations.title: Impossible.
annotations.text: [1] How hard the holy Scriptures be, and how dangerously they be read of the vnlearned, or of the proud be they neuer so wel learned, this one place might teach vs. [2] Wherat the Nouatians of old did so stumble, that they thought, and heretically taught, that none falling into any mortal sinne after Baptisme, could be receiued to mercie or penance in the Church: and so to a contentious man, that would folow his owne sense, or the bare wordes, without regard of the Churches sense and rule of faith (after which euery Scripture must be expounded) the Apostles speach doth here sound. [3] Euen as to the simple, and to the Heretike that submitteth not his sense to the Churches iudgement, certaine places of this same Epistle, seeme at the first sight, to stand against the daily oblation or sacrifice of the Masse: which yet in truth make no more for that purpose, then this text we now stand on, serueth the Nouatians: as when we come to the places, it shal be declared. And let the good Readers beware here also of the Protestants exposition, for they are herein worse then Nouatians, specially such as precisely folow Caluin: [4] holding impiously, that it is impossible for one that forsaketh entirely his faith, that is, becommeth an Apostata or an Heretike, to be receiued to penance or to Gods mercie. To establish which false and damnable sense, these fellowes make nothing of S. Ambroses, S. Chrysostoms, and the other fathers exposition, [5]which is the holy Churches sense, [6] That the Apostle meaneth of that penance which is done before and in Baptisme. which is no more to say, but that it is impossible to be baptized againe, and thereby to be renouated and illuminated, to die, be buried, and rise againe the second time in Christ, in so easie and perfect penance and cleansing of sinnes, as that first sacrament of generation did yeld: which applieth Christes death in such ample maner to the receiuers, that it taketh away al paines due for sinnes before committed: and therfore requireth no further penance afterward, for the sinnes before committed, al being washed away by the force of that Sacrament duely taken. S. Augustine calleth the remission in Baptisme, Magnam indulgentiam, a great pardon. Enchirid. c. 64. [7] The Apostle therfore warneth them, that if they fall from their faith, and from Christes grace and law which they once receiued in their Baptisme, they may not looke to haue any more that first great and large remedie applied vnto them, nor no man els that sinneth after Baptisme: though the other penance, which is called the Second table after sinners shipwracke, [8]which is a more paineful medicine for sinne then Baptisme, requiring much fasting, praying, and other afflictions corporal, is open not onely to other sinners, but to al once baptized, Heretikes, or oppugners of the truth malitiously and of purpose or what way so euer, during this life. See S. Cyprian ep. 52. S. Ambrose vpon this place. S. Augustine cont. ep. Parm. li. 2. c. 13. and ep. 50. S. Damascene li. 4. c. 10.

notes.text: The Nouatians (as al Heretikes) made Scripture the ground of their heresie.

annotations.title: God is not vniust.
annotations.text: ◦ It is a world to see, what wringing & writhing the Protestants make, to shift them selues from the euidence of these wordes, which make it most cleere to all not blinded in pride and contention, that good workes be meritorious, and the very cause of saluation, so far, that God should be vniust, if he rendered not heauen for the same. Reuera grandis iniustitia Dei (saith S. Hierom) Si tantum peccata puniret, & bona opera non susciperet. That is, In deede great were Gods iniustice, if he would onely punish sinnes, and would not receiue good workes. Li. 2. cont. Iouin. c. 2.

notes.text: Gods iustice in rewarding meritorious workes.
